Tshirt Workshop · Staff guide

Graphic Engine

Graphic Engine gets artwork ready for DTF printing. Open a design, tell it the print size, pick a print style, check it, save it. Most jobs take four clicks.

Open it in your browser 24davo.github.io/tsw-dn-assets/halftone Nothing is uploaded. The art stays on your computer.
  1. Open a design and set the size
  2. Choose the print style
  3. Speed buttons and Presets
  4. Fine-tune, only if needed

  6. Trace prep for Illustrator

The screen at a glance

  • 1Open art and Save PNG. The file name, print size and a sharpness badge sit to the left.
  • 2Tabs. Each design you open gets its own tab. An amber dot means it isn’t saved yet.
  • 3View and Shirt. Change how you look at the print, and the shirt colour it sits on.
  • 4Before on the left, After on the right. The dashed line is the edge of the print.
  • 5Zoom, and two buttons you hold down to flick back to the Original or see it Transparent.
  • 6Tools. Speed buttons at the top, then three numbered steps. Everything else is under Fine-tune.

The tool is dark so colours are easy to judge, like Photoshop. Light mode at the top switches it if you prefer.

1

Open a design and set the size

  1. Click Open art and choose the file. You can also drag files onto the page, or paste a picture. PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF and SVG all open.
  2. Open 1 Print size. Click Chest 90, Front 280 or Back 330, or type the width or the height in mm. The other box follows.
  3. Look at the badge beside the file name. Green means the file is sharp enough at that size.

Always set the size first. The dots are worked out at the real print size. If you change the size later, the tool redraws them, which is fine. What you must never do is resize a saved file in another program. The dots would change size with it.

The largest print is 400 × 500 mm, either way round. The tool won’t go past it.

What the tool tells you here

“No size is saved in this file”The file doesn’t know how big it should print. Pick a size. Until you do, the check list keeps reminding you.
“Upscale needed”The file is too small for that size and will print soft. The note says how much to enlarge it, or how wide it can print as it is. If it’s far too small, ask the customer for a bigger file or vector art.
“There’s empty space around the art”Click Trim to the art. The size then measures the design, not the blank margin.
“JPEG · check”The JPG was saved at low quality. Zoom in and look for blocky patches before you go on.
2

Choose the print style

DTF film can’t print ink that is half see-through. Every spot is either solid ink or clear film. So soft shading (a glow, a shadow, a fade) has to become one of two things: tiny solid dots, or a clean hard edge. That is the choice you make here.

Halftone

Shading becomes dots

For photos, glows, smoke, flames and anything that fades into the shirt. Halftone means tiny solid dots that look like shading from arm’s length.

Clean cut

Solid ink, no dots

For logos, lettering and bold art. Soft edges print fully solid or are removed, so the outline is crisp.

Prep only

Tidy up and save

For a normal picture that needs no dots. Set the size, remove the background, tidy the edge, touch up, save.

Trace prep

Flat colours for tracing

Not a print file. It flattens a logo into clean flat colours so Illustrator’s Image Trace gives tidy shapes. See step 6.

Then a Quick start

Under the four buttons is a short list called Quick start. It sets how the style treats the design. Click one and watch the After side.

Shadows to dotsHalftone. Only the deepest shadows turn into dots. Colours stay strong. This is the one the tool starts on.
Fix soft edgesHalftone. Only glows, soft shadows and fades turn into dots. Solid parts stay solid.
Shirt shows throughHalftone. Colours close to the shirt colour drop out, and shading turns into dots. Lighter to wear.
Full halftoneHalftone. The whole design becomes dots, for a soft vintage look.
Remove shadowsClean cut. A quick clean-up for dark shirts. Shadows drop out and the rest prints solid.
Knock out the shirt colourClean cut. Colours close to the shirt colour drop out. Everything else prints solid.
Clean up onlyClean cut. Nothing is removed by colour. Soft edges just go solid or go away.

Click the Shirt colour at the top of the preview first. Several Quick starts work from it.

3

Speed buttons and Presets

This is the quick way in. One click sets the print style, the Quick start and the dots for an everyday job. Check the print size after.

Speed buttons

They sit at the very top of Tools, on two tabs.

Built inQuick clean cut, Black tee, White tee, Coloured tee, Dark photo on black, Glows & soft shadows. The same on every computer.
OursSix buttons the workshop sets up itself. Click + Add on an empty one, choose what it does and name it. They are shared with every workshop computer.

Quick clean cut does three jobs at once: Clean cut with a hard edge, the background removed, and the file trimmed to the art. It’s the fastest way to prep a logo.

Presets

Open Presets and choose from the list. It has more choices than the buttons, in groups:

Starters · 30 lpiThirteen built-in set-ups for black, white and coloured tees. Each one shows a short note saying what it’s for when you pick it.
Claude recipesSet-ups worked out on a real job. The first is “Elefus · flames fade, skull stays solid”: red flames fade into a black tee, and the grey skull stays solid.
Shared with all computersPresets staff have saved and shared.
This computer onlyPresets saved here and not shared yet.

To keep a set-up you like, click Save new and name it. Share with all computers sends it to the others. Sharing asks for the team code once on each computer. It’s in the Settings tab of the “DTF Halftone Presets” Google Sheet.

The list only shows presets for the print style you’re in. Starters and Claude recipes show in Halftone.

Treat halftone set-ups as a starting point Most Starters and recipes were tuned on screen and have not been through a real print and wash yet. For a big or fussy job, print a small test first. The dot sizes come from the Dot limits buttons in Ink density, and there’s a test chart linked there to check them on our printer and film.
4

Fine-tune, only if needed

Click Fine-tune to open the rest of the tools. Leave it shut if the design already looks right. A number beside it shows how many sections you’ve changed.

Every section has a short note, a More link for the longer one, and a Reset link that puts just that section back. Hover over anything for a tip.

Background

Remove the background is for JPGs and screenshots on a plain colour. It clears that colour only where it touches the outside edge, so white inside the design (text, eyes, highlights) stays.

  • Bits of design going too? Lower Tolerance. Background left behind? Raise it.
  • Background shut inside a letter, like the middle of an O, stays. Brush it out with the Eraser in Touch up.

Make see-through areas solid is for AI art. Many AI images look solid but are partly see-through. They print dark on a dark tee and faint on a light one. The check list warns you: “52% of the design is partly see-through”.

  • Tick the box, then choose how the design should look: as it does on White, on Black, or on The shirt colour.
  • Show the see-through areas shows you where they are.
  • If a faint smudge around the design turns into a solid patch, raise Leave out anything fainter than.

Leave it off for real glows, shadows and fades. Those are meant to be soft, and Halftone turns them into dots.

Parts

Parts give one piece of the design its own treatment. Click Add a part, then:

  1. Pick it. By tone or colour (Shadows, Midtones, Highlights, Greys, black & white, or Sampled colours you click on the art), or choose Everything and Paint or Box the area.
  2. Say what happens to it. Remove, Fade to dots, Own dots, Keep solid, No dots, Main dots, or Recolour.

Show lights up what the part covers. On switches it off and on so you can compare.

Grey skull in red smokePick Greys, black & white, then Keep solid or No dots. The smoke gets dots, the skull doesn’t.
Black text on a black teePick the text colour with Sampled colours, then Recolour to white.
One word must stay solidChoose Everything, Box the word, then Keep solid.

Edge, and Fade the edge

The Edge section tidies the outline.

Hard edgeHalftone only. Soft edges print fully solid or are removed, for a crisp outline. Untick it to keep a glow as dots.
Crisp outlinesOn already. Keeps lettering and sharp lines clean, not broken up by dots.
Speck clean-upOn already. Removes specks too small to print and fills pinholes.
Fade the edgeHalftone only. Breaks the outline into dots over the distance you set, up to 20 mm. Inward keeps the print the same size. Good for a photo with a hard rectangle edge. The two Outward choices trail dots past the outline, so the print gets bigger. Outward has not been proven in print yet, so test it first.
Trim the edgeShaves the outline in by a few pixels. 1 px is 0.08 mm. Any colour clears the pale fringe left after a background removal.
Shirt-colour edgeAdds a thin edge in the shirt colour to hold fine or broken detail together. Keep it thin.

Brightness & levels

Use this before anything else if the art is too dark or flat.

  • Brightness and Contrast work like Photoshop’s. Double-click a slider to put it back to 0.
  • Colours going grey or washed out? Tick Keep colour strength.
  • Levels: drag the black triangle right and more of the art counts as shadow. On a black tee that means more of it drops out or turns to dots. Auto has a go for you.

Touch up

Three brushes you drag on the preview.

EraserClears stray pixels and leftover background.
PaintFills gaps. Alt-click the art to pick up a colour.
RestoreBrings the original back where you brush.

[ and ] change the brush size. Hold Space to move around. Esc puts the brush down.

The other sections, in one line each

CropTrim to the art, or draw your own crop.
Halftone dotsHow fine the dots are. 30 lpi (lines per inch) is our everyday setting. 35 is finer and may need more care.
SharpenLight or Medium brings back crispness in a soft file.
Knock outWhich colour drops out to the shirt, and how far the fade runs.
Ink densityDot limits: Fine, Standard, Extra safe. Standard suits most prints.
Ink colourFull colour or one colour. Leave “Allow for DTF black ink” on. Our black ink prints as a dark grey, and the preview shows that.
5

Check and save

Read the check list

Open 3 Check & save. Each line is a check the tool has done for you.

✓ Green tickGood. Nothing to do.
! Amber markRead it. It says what’s wrong and where to fix it. The step title shows how many there are, like “2 to check”.
Grey symbolJust telling you what was done, like “Background removed”.

Look at it properly

  • 1:1 (bottom right) before every save. The Fit view can show patterns that aren’t really in the file.
  • Life size shows the print at its real size on your screen. The first time, click the small ruler button beside it and match the box to a bank card (85.6 mm wide). Do that once on each screen.
  • On shirt shows the print on the shirt colour. Click a Shirt swatch to try another colour.
  • Hold Original to flick back to the art as it came in.

The other views

SplitBefore and After side by side. Each side has a menu to choose what it shows.
TransparentThe print on a checkerboard, so you can see every bit that was removed.
On whiteThe print over plain white.
White baseWhere the white ink goes under the colour.
Ink mapWhite is solid ink, pink is dots, grey was removed.

Save

Click Save PNG at the top, or Done · Save PNG at the bottom of the check list. The file is a 300 dpi PNG at the exact print size. With several tabs open, Save all saves every one.

The tool names the file for you, so anyone can tell what it is later:

club-logo_twedit_280w_30lpi_order-57615.png
  • club-logoThe name of the file you opened.
  • _tweditOur mark. It’s been through Graphic Engine and is ready to print.
  • _280wThe print is 280 mm wide.
  • _30lpiHalftone, with dots at 30 lines per inch. Clean cut and Prep only files leave this out.
  • _order-57615Anything you type in “Add to the file name”. Optional.

Trace prep files end in _trace (or _flat with the tracing background off). Those are for Illustrator, not for printing.

If you used an outward fade, the width in the name includes the fade.

6

Trace prep for Illustrator

Use this when a customer sends a small or fuzzy logo and you want clean vector shapes. Image Trace struggles with fuzzy edges and off-whites. Trace prep fixes the picture first, so the trace comes out clean.

  1. Open the logo. Set the print size to 250 mm or more on the long side. A bigger size traces with smoother curves. Ignore “Upscale needed” here.
  2. Click Trace prep in Print style.
  3. If the logo is on a plain background, open Fine-tune, then Background, and tick Remove the background.
  4. Open Flat colours and check the colour squares. Auto counts the colours for you. If it found too many, click the right number, or click a square to leave that colour out.
  5. Click Save PNG. The file name ends in _trace.
  6. In Illustrator, place the PNG and run Image Trace. Ask for the number of colours the tool tells you.
  7. Delete the background shape. Done.

Why one more colour?

Background for tracing puts a solid colour behind the logo in the saved file, with a small margin. With nothing see-through, Image Trace has no faint edge to turn into stray outlines. That background counts as a colour, so a 3-colour logo needs 4 in Image Trace. The tool always tells you the number.

AutoPicks a colour far from every colour in the logo, often a bright pink or green. Leave it here unless you have a reason.
Black, White, OwnChoose the background yourself. The tool warns you if it’s too close to a logo colour.
OffNo background. The file stays transparent and the name ends in _flat. Ask for the logo’s own number of colours.

The three tidy-up sliders

Pure white and pure blackTicked already. Nearly-white becomes true white and nearly-black true black.
Smooth jagged edgesEvens out stair-steps on a low-res logo. Starts at 4. If small text is blobbing, lower it.
Tidy bits smaller thanMelts specks and thin in-between lines into the colour beside them. Starts at 0.5 mm. Raise it for a rough scan.
Still new Trace prep has been tested on made-up logos, not yet on a full run through Illustrator. Check the traced result against the customer’s original. Gradients come out as steps, so it suits flat logos, not shaded art.
7

Which one do I pick?

The jobClick thisGood to know
Photo on a black teeSpeed button Black teeDark backgrounds melt into the shirt with no box. Dim phone photo? Use Dark photo on black.
Logo with soft edgesSpeed button Quick clean cutCrisp edge, background gone, trimmed. If the soft part is a glow or drop shadow the customer wants, use Glows & soft shadows.
AI artOpen it and read the check list firstIf it warns the design is partly see-through and it should be solid, tick Make see-through areas solid in Background. Then choose the button for the tee.
Flames or smokePresets: Black tee · long fade (flames, smoke, glows)Skull, metal or lettering that must stay solid? Use long fade, greys stay solid, or the Elefus recipe. People in smoke? Use smoke fades, people stay solid.
White teeSpeed button White teeWhite in the design becomes the shirt. For skies and clouds try the preset White tee · halftone fade. Art made for dark tees can break up on white.
Coloured teeClick the Shirt colour, then speed button Coloured teeThe safe choice for photos and faces.
Photo with a hard rectangle edgePresets: Boxed picture · soft dotted edgeThe picture stays solid and its edge fades into the shirt through 8 mm of dots.
Normal picture, no dots neededPrint style Prep onlySize, background, edge, touch up, save.
Logo to tracePrint style Trace prepSize 250 mm or more. Ask Image Trace for the number of colours the tool gives you.

Not sure? Click a few speed buttons and Starters and watch the After side. Nothing is lost. Undo takes you back.

8

If something looks wrong

I’ve made a mess of itUndo, or open History and click an earlier step. Revert at the top of Tools goes back to the design as it opened. Reset to defaults puts the tool’s own settings back.
The preview is stuck on “Updating…”Wait a few seconds and a Redraw link appears. Click it. If it stays stuck, the tool restarts the preview by itself.
The badge says “Upscale needed”The file is too small for the size. Open Print size and follow the note: enlarge it in your upscaler, ask for a bigger file, or print it smaller.
A soft glow turned into a solid ringHard edge is on. The tee Starters switch it on. Use Glows & soft shadows, or untick Hard edge in the Edge section.
Parts of the design disappearedThey are close to the shirt colour, so they were knocked out. In Halftone choose Fix soft edges. In Clean cut choose Clean up only. Or add a part and choose Keep solid.
The design looks dull or half missing on a dark shirtIt’s probably partly see-through. Read the check list, then tick Make see-through areas solid in Background.
Black looks dark grey in the previewThat’s correct. DTF black ink prints as a dark matt grey, never as black as a black tee. The tool shows it honestly.
Fades on a black tee look muddyIn Brightness & levels, drag the black triangle to about 40. Still muddy? Tick Rich fade dots in Knock out. Clean colour dots is stronger again, with a bolder, more cartoon look.
A pale fringe after removing the backgroundEdge section: Trim the edge, Any colour, 2 to 4 px.
Background colour left inside lettersIt only clears from the outside edge. Use the Eraser in Touch up.
Check list: “Smallest dot about 0.2 mm”Dots that small can wash off. In Ink density click Standard or Extra safe.
I can’t find a presetThe list only shows presets for the print style you’re in. Starters and Claude recipes show in Halftone only.
Life size isn’t the real sizeClick the ruler button beside Life size and set it up again with a bank card. Each screen needs its own set-up.
The page closed or refreshedOpen it again. Your tabs come back as you left them, with Undo. A tab you closed yourself stays closed.
Traced logo has wobbly or stepped edgesMake the print size bigger, and raise Smooth jagged edges in Flat colours.

Handy keys

  • V step through the views
  • O hold to see the original
  • T flick to Transparent
  • E print edge on or off
  • + − 0 zoom in, out, fit
  • Cmd/Ctrl Z undo
Written for Graphic Engine version 73, November 2026. Screenshots show the tool’s own sample art and a made-up test logo. If a button here doesn’t match what you see, the tool has been updated: trust the tool, and let the owner know so the guide gets fixed.
